stops.note: compound of iye ("mother"), ọmọ ("child"), and ẹja ("fish"): "mother whose children are like the fish"
stops.meaning: river goddess of motherhood and creation

stops.note: creolized in Cuba as enslaved Yoruba carried her worship into Santería/Lucumí practice
stops.meaning: orisha of the sea and motherhood in Santería

stops.note: spread into English through Santería and wider diaspora spiritual writing
stops.meaning: orisha and goddess of the sea and motherhood

current_meaning: the Yoruba-derived orisha of the sea and motherhood, venerated across Santería and other diaspora religions
